Coursol, P., Mackey, P.J., Kapusta, J.P.T. and Cardona Valencia, N. (2015). Energy Consumption in Copper Smelting: A New Asian Horse in the Race. JOM (The Minerals, Metals & Materials Society). doi:10.1007/s11837-015-1380-1

Locators are PDF pages (the PDF carries no printed page numbers; Table I-II on PDF p.6, Tables III-V on p.8). Main file: seven concentrate-to-anode-copper routes, fuel in MJ/t anode copper and net electricity in kWh/t. Noranda and BBS electricity are printed in kWh/t (Tables III, IV). Table V prints electricity only as MJ/t fuel-equivalent at 38% power plant efficiency, so the other five routes carry derived kWh/t (MJ*0.38/3.6, formula column; the conversion reproduces Table III exactly). Table V also holds other-values primary totals. Rows for flash, Isasmelt, Mitsubishi, Noranda-Teniente are reprinted from Coursol, Mackey and Diaz 2010 (Copper 2010); reverberatory from Kellogg and Henderson 1976. Individual unit-operation kWh (oxygen, air, acid plant) only in other-values for oxygen; Table I unit parameters not loaded. No costs or emissions. Capacity of the Dongying BBS furnace loaded.

to-get.csv lists this paper as JOM 64(11) 2012; the title page printed here is (c) 2015 with DOI 10.1007/s11837-015-1380-1, so 2015 was used. Energies are modelled (Metsim) on one standard concentrate, not plant data. Net electricity is after a steam credit that assumes surplus steam generates power.
